A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the mutagenic action of N4- aminocytidine is due to the incorporation of this compound into DNA, but the incorporation is not the only factor in determining the mutation frequency; the mutagenicity is also dependent on the metabolic pathway of N4-ami- nocytidine in cells.

N4- aminocytidine is a mutagenic nucleosidic analog which can be taken up by E. coli cells and incorporated into their DNA as N4-amino- deoxycytosine; the mutagenic action of this analog is probably due to mispairing between N4-aminodC and guanosine.
the mutagenicity of N4-amine-cytidine is due to its incorporation into DNA as N(4)-aminodeoxycytidine, which is formed by an enzymatic pathway that includes deamination of the N4-amine group.

the N4-amino group is a good site for introducing a chemical group into the cytosine molecule that can be used to probe its role in DNA replication and mutagenesis.
